scenarios.customerLine: The display says 'Replace UV lamp' — what do I do?
scenarios.repResponse: I'll order you a replacement lamp and send a 2-minute install guide. Done.
scenarios.intent: Rep resolved it directly. Known issue, clear fix. No reason to interrupt.

scenarios.customerLine: Water tastes a bit off lately.
scenarios.repResponse: Sounds like the filter cycle. I'm scheduling a filter swap and crediting this month.
scenarios.intent: Standard resolution path. Rep is in control. Stay out of the way.

scenarios.customerLine: I was overcharged last month, I want it fixed now.
scenarios.repResponse: I see the double charge — refunding it now, you'll see it in 3 days.
scenarios.intent: Billing fix within rep's authority. Confident, resolved. Silence is the right call.

scenarios.customerLine: Can I add a second unit for my office on the same account?
scenarios.repResponse: Absolutely — adding it now to your business profile.
scenarios.intent: Upsell handled cleanly. This is a win, not a friction point.

scenarios.customerLine: I don't want to talk to you. Put your manager on. Now.
scenarios.repResponse: I understand — I'd really like to help you myself first...
scenarios.customerEscalation: No. Manager. I'm not repeating myself again.
scenarios.trigger: Two consecutive manager demands + rep refusal loop detected.
scenarios.screenNote: Customer demanding manager. You're not stuck — I've got you. Don't decide. Read this if needed: 'I hear you. I'm bringing in my manager Dana, who already has the full picture.'
scenarios.managerBrief: Hi Dana, Warm Transfer here. Noa has a customer on the line who's asked for a manager twice — billing dispute from last month, already partially handled, customer is frustrated and doesn't want to repeat himself. You have the full context. Ready to take over warmly whenever you are.
scenarios.intent: Two refusals = real escalation. Rep is at the freeze point. Act now: brief the manager, hand Noa the words, bridge only if the wall holds.
